briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Ann Arbor Stays Open For Business as Michigan Operators Find Workarounds — While DC Pushes Rescheduling and Psychedelics Toward the Finish Line
briefs.top: Michigan operators are proving they can out-hustle the 24% wholesale tax — new storefronts, out-of-state expansion, and supplier cost-sharing deals are keeping the state's legal market moving, while both major gubernatorial candidates now back tax relief. Nationally, the DEA's rescheduling hearing and a stacked FDA psychedelics calendar are turning 2026 into the most consequential policy year the plant-medicine industry has seen in decades.

local.text: Blue Sky Cannabis Co. quietly opened in downtown Ann Arbor right next to Spores Cafe, giving the city a fresh storefront and a built-in mushroom-cafe crossover crowd for cross-promotion.

Michigan-based JARS Cannabis is building an out-of-state growth engine, announcing a deal to acquire Sonoran Roots and its eight Ponderosa-brand dispensaries — a move that will make JARS the largest dispensary chain in Arizona.

Despite the wholesale tax shock, statewide sales have stabilized rather than collapsed: after bottoming in January, monthly revenue climbed back to $255.4 million by March and held steady near $253.5 million through June — proof the market found a floor.

Tax relief now has bipartisan momentum heading into November: GOP nominee John James is pledging to cut the cannabis excise tax and roll back the wholesale levy, while Democratic candidates including Chris Swanson have vowed to repeal the 24% tax outright, calling it "not fair and equitable."

The tax is squeezing the U.P. hard — Higher Love closed five of its nine Upper Michigan stores — but three-location operator Rize is showing the playbook forward, sustaining growth by negotiating cost-sharing arrangements that split the tax burden with suppliers instead of absorbing it alone.

national.text: The DEA's marijuana rescheduling process hit a critical procedural checkpoint this week, continuing forward momentum toward Schedule III — a shift that would eliminate the punishing IRS Section 280E tax burden for state-licensed operators.

FDA finalized its first-ever clinical trial guidance for psilocybin, LSD and MDMA and locked in a September 14 public hearing on therapeutic psychedelics — building, as one analysis put it, "the institutional infrastructure for what may soon become a live approval docket."

Compass Pathways is targeting a Q4 2026 NDA submission for its psilocybin therapy COMP360, after FDA handed it a National Priority Voucher in April that compresses review time from roughly a year down to just weeks — putting a real depression-treatment approval within sight this year.

Curaleaf's takeover bid for Aurora Cannabis is moving forward — a $4-per-share, 45%-premium offer that would create a combined company with $1.5 billion-plus in pro forma revenue and signals major MSOs are now thinking cross-border.

Consolidation keeps accelerating: Vireo Growth closed its $49 million PharmaCann Colorado acquisition and is pushing ahead with its Planet 13 merger, assembling what could become the largest dispensary portfolio in the country by store count.
